summary: Add crate favorites, a user-to-crate relation modelled on Follows. T1 builds the backend in one pass: shared Zod contract, the crate_favorites table and generated migration 0006, a favorites service, PUT/DELETE /api/crates/:id/favorite, viewerFavorited on GET /api/crates/:id, a favorites array on the public profile, and API and migration tests. Once T1 lands, two web tasks with separate files run in parallel. T2 adds the Favorite toggle to the single-crate page. T3 adds the Favorites section to the profile and updates the docs.

tasks.goal: Backend for crate favorites: shared contract, crate_favorites table and migration 0006, service, routes, viewerFavorited on GET /crates/:id, favorites on the public profile, and API and migration tests.
tasks.description:
Template: the Follows feature (apps/api/src/routes/follows.ts, apps/api/src/services/follows.ts, the follows table in apps/api/src/db/schema.ts, apps/api/test/follows.test.ts). Favorites mirror it as user->crate.

1. SHARED CONTRACT (packages/shared/src/index.ts)
- Add, near profileCrate:
```ts
// Data classification: PUBLIC. A crate someone favorited, as their profile lists it. Owner username and display name only (null for ownerless legacy crates). No owner id.
export const profileFavorite = z.object({
  id: z.number().int(),
  name: z.string(),
  color: z.string(),
  label: z.string().nullable(),
  albumCount: z.number().int(),
  ownerUsername: z.string().nullable(),
  ownerDisplayName: z.string().nullable(),
})
```
- Add `favorites: z.array(profileFavorite)` to publicProfile, right after `crates`. Doc comment: newest favorited first.
- Add `export const crateDetail = crate.extend({ viewerFavorited: z.boolean() })` with the comment 'Does the signed-in viewer favorite this crate? Always false when signed out.'
- Export the types `ProfileFavorite` and `CrateDetail` (z.infer) beside ProfileCrate and Crate.

2. DB (apps/api/src/db/schema.ts)
- Add after follows:
```ts
// Data classification: INTERNAL (personal data: which crates a user favorited). Profiles show a user's favorites as public crate cards; numeric ids never leave the API.
// 'cascade' = deleting the user or the crate deletes the favorite rows.
export const crateFavorites = sqliteTable('crate_favorites', {
  id: integer('id').primaryKey({ autoIncrement: true }),
  userId: integer('user_id').notNull().references(() => users.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }),
  crateId: integer('crate_id').notNull().references(() => crates.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }),
  createdAt: timestamps.createdAt,
}, (t) => [
  uniqueIndex('crate_favorites_user_crate_unique').on(t.userId, t.crateId),
  index('crate_favorites_crate_idx').on(t.crateId),
])
```
  Add relations entries if the file has relations blocks for follows.
- Generate the migration with `npm run db:generate -w apps/api -- --name crate_favorites`. This writes apps/api/drizzle/0006_crate_favorites.sql, meta/0006_snapshot.json and the _journal.json entry. Never hand-write or hand-edit them. Do not touch 0000-0005. The SQL must only CREATE TABLE and CREATE INDEX, with no table rebuilds.
- Check apps/api/test/dev-admin.test.ts, apps/api/scripts/check-dev-admin.ts, apps/api/test/demo-seed.test.ts, apps/api/test/schema.test.ts, src/db/backup.ts, src/db/restore.ts and src/services/admin.ts for hard-coded table lists. Add crate_favorites wherever the follows table is enumerated.

3. SERVICE: new file apps/api/src/services/favorites.ts
- `favoriteCrate(db: Db, viewer: PublicUser | null, crateId: number): void`: requireUser(viewer) (401). Select crate {id, ownerId}; if it is missing, throw notFound(`Crate ${crateId}`) (404). If crate.ownerId === signedIn.id, throw badRequest('You cannot favorite your own crate') (400). Then insert with .onConflictDoNothing(). Ownerless (null owner) crates and other users' crates are allowed, including for admins. 404 is checked before 400.
- `unfavoriteCrate(db, viewer, crateId): void`: requireUser, 404 if the crate is missing, otherwise delete the row for (viewer, crate). A missing row is a no-op.
- `isFavoritedBy(db, crateId: number, viewerId: number | null): boolean`: false when viewerId is null.
- `listFavorites(db, userId: number): ProfileFavorite[]`: from crateFavorites innerJoin crates, leftJoin users on users.id = crates.ownerId, leftJoin albums on albums.crateId = crates.id. Select exactly id, name, color, label, albumCount: count(albums.id), ownerUsername: users.username, ownerDisplayName: users.displayName. where crateFavorites.userId = userId, groupBy crates.id, orderBy desc(crateFavorites.createdAt), desc(crateFavorites.id). Never select email, role, user ids or demoSeedKey.
- Write a data-classification header comment like the one in services/follows.ts.

4. ROUTES: new file apps/api/src/routes/favorites.ts, registered in apps/api/src/app.ts the way followRoutes is (same prefix).
- PUT /crates/:id/favorite and DELETE /crates/:id/favorite, each `{ schema: { params: idParams }, preValidation: signedInOnly }`, returning reply.code(204).send(). Define signedInOnly locally as in follows.ts (`async (req) => { requireUser(req.user) }`). Because it runs in preValidation, a signed-out caller gets 401 even with a non-numeric id. Check that /crates/:id/favorite does not collide with /crates/order or /crates/recommended in crates.ts.
- GET /crates/:id in apps/api/src/routes/crates.ts: response schema becomes crateDetail, and the handler calls a new `getCrateDetail(db: Db, id: number, viewer: PublicUser | null): CrateDetail` in apps/api/src/services/crates.ts. It returns `{ ...getCrate(db, id), viewerFavorited: isFavoritedBy(db, id, viewer?.id ?? null) }`. Keep getCrate unchanged, because create, update and delete use it. GET /crates (the list) stays as it is.

5. PROFILE (apps/api/src/services/profiles.ts)
- toPublicProfile adds `favorites: listFavorites(db, user.id)` after `crates`. profileCrates stays owner-only. Favorites are PUBLIC: any viewer, signed in or not, sees them. updateOwnProfile and setVerified return toPublicProfile, so they gain the field too. Fix any existing toEqual assertions on those responses.

6. WEB FIXTURES. Adding a required `favorites` breaks typecheck in the web test fixtures that build a PublicProfile. Add `favorites: []` to the fixtures in apps/web/src/views/ProfileView.test.ts, apps/web/src/views/MyProfileView.test.ts, apps/web/src/views/EditProfileView.test.ts and apps/web/src/stores/session.test.ts. Make no other web changes. In apps/web/src/views/ProfileView.vue, do not add UI yet. T3 does that.

7. TESTS
- apps/api/test/migration.test.ts (AC1): add a 'migration 0006' describe that follows the existing 0005 test pattern. (a) A fresh DB through createDb has crate_favorites. (b) Build a DB at 0005 holding users and crates, then open it so 0006 applies; every pre-existing user and crate row is still there. In both cases check: PRAGMA index_list shows a unique index on (user_id, crate_id), and PRAGMA foreign_key_list(crate_favorites) shows on_delete 'CASCADE' for both the users and crates FKs. Add an 'only adds to the schema' test for 0006 that mirrors the 0005 one.
- New apps/api/test/favorites.test.ts, using buildTestApp and helpers.ts as follows.test.ts does:
  - AC2: PUT gives 204, and repeating it gives 204 with exactly one row. DELETE gives 204 and removes the row, and repeating it gives 204.
  - AC3: PUT on your own crate gives 400 and writes no row. Signed-out PUT gives 401, also for /crates/abc/favorite. Unknown id gives 404. Signed-out DELETE gives 401.
  - AC4: GET /api/crates/:id viewerFavorited is true for the favoriter, false for another signed-in user and false signed out.
  - Admins can favorite another user's crate. Ownerless crates can be favorited.
  - AC5: GET /api/users/:username has favorites newest first (control createdAt, or rely on the id tiebreak), and each entry's keys are exactly [id, name, label, color, albumCount, ownerUsername, ownerDisplayName]. The crates array has only owned crates, and a favorited crate is not in it. The serialized body contains no 'email', 'role', 'demoSeedKey' or numeric user id fields.
  - AC6: deleting a favorited empty crate through DELETE /api/crates/:id removes the favorite rows, and the favoriter's profile favorites no longer list it. Deleting the favoriting user (db.delete(users) directly; there is no route for it) removes their rows. Crate delete still returns 204, so the cascade does not block it.
- Fix any existing API tests (profiles, shared-profile, crates, schema) that break on the new fields.

Run `npm test`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` from the repo root, and `npx prettier --check` on the files you change. Do not start a dev server or touch data/crate.db. Commits: Conventional Commits, e.g. feat(api): ..., feat(shared): ...

tasks.goal: Favorite toggle on the single-crate page /crates/:id, shown only to a signed-in viewer who does not own the crate, with component tests.
tasks.description:
API (built by T1, already merged):
- PUT /api/crates/:id/favorite and DELETE /api/crates/:id/favorite both return 204 and are idempotent. They return 401 when signed out, 400 when PUT targets your own crate, and 404 for an unknown crate.
- GET /api/crates/:id returns `CrateDetail` from '@frisson/shared' = Crate & { viewerFavorited: boolean }. Crate has id, name, color, label, sortBy, sortOrder, albumCount, ownerId: number | null, ownerUsername, ownerDisplayName.

Build:
1. apps/web/src/api/favorites.ts, modelled on apps/web/src/api/follows.ts: `favoriteCrate(id: number) => request<void>(`/crates/${id}/favorite`, { method: 'PUT' })` and `unfavoriteCrate(id: number)` with DELETE. Add a data-classification comment.
2. apps/web/src/api/crates.ts: add `getCrate(id: number) => request<CrateDetail>(`/crates/${id}`)`.
3. apps/web/src/components/crate/FavoriteButton.vue, modelled on apps/web/src/components/profile/FollowButton.vue (not optimistic: busy and error state; emits only after the server agrees).
   - Props `{ crateId: number; favorited: boolean }`. Emits `changed: [favorited: boolean]`.
   - A `<button type="button">` whose accessible name is exactly 'Favorite' in both states, with `:aria-pressed="favorited"`. A decorative star glyph may sit in an aria-hidden span. Style the pressed state visibly, using the existing tokens (--ink, --paper, --marker-red).
   - Clicking calls favoriteCrate when not pressed and unfavoriteCrate when pressed. On success it emits changed(!favorited), guarding against the crateId changing mid-request as FollowButton does. On failure it shows a role=alert message via errorMessage and aria-pressed stays as it was.
4. apps/web/src/views/CrateView.vue:
   - `showFavorite = props.crateId !== undefined && library.status === 'ready' && !!session.user && !!crate.value && crate.value.ownerId !== session.user.id`. Ownerless crates (ownerId null) show it, and admins see it on others' crates. It never shows on /shelf (no crateId), on your own crate, or when signed out. There is no 'log in to favorite' link.
   - Hold `viewerFavorited = ref<boolean | null>(null)`. Watch [props.crateId, session.user?.id, showFavorite]. When showFavorite is true, call getCrate(crateId) and set viewerFavorited from the response. Otherwise reset it to null. Ignore stale responses whose crateId or user no longer matches. On a fetch error, leave it null so the button stays hidden.
   - Render `<FavoriteButton v-if="showFavorite && viewerFavorited !== null" :crate-id="crate.id" :favorited="viewerFavorited" @changed="viewerFavorited = $event" />` next to the OwnerLink under the crate name. It must not overflow at 390px wide. Leave the existing toolbar, crate actions, edit gating and spin logic as they are.
5. Tests:
   - New apps/web/src/components/crate/FavoriteButton.test.ts.
   - In apps/web/src/views/CrateView.test.ts (AC8): a signed-in non-owner sees the button 'Favorite' with aria-pressed matching viewerFavorited (true and false cases). The same holds for an admin viewing another user's crate. The button is absent on the viewer's own crate, when signed out, and on /shelf. Clicking calls PUT /api/crates/:id/favorite when unpressed and DELETE when pressed, and aria-pressed flips only after the mocked request resolves. A failed request leaves it unchanged.
   - The tests mock global fetch and count '/api/crates' calls. The new GET /api/crates/:id call may break existing fetch mocks in CrateView.test.ts, crateActions.test.ts and editControls.test.ts. Update those mocks so they route by URL rather than by call order, and keep every existing assertion's meaning.

Conventions: Vue 3 script setup + TS, Prettier with no semicolons, single quotes, width 100. Render user text with {{ }} only. Run `npm test -w apps/web`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` from the repo root. Do not start a dev server or touch data/crate.db or .shipyard/. Commit as feat(web): ...

tasks.goal: Favorites section on the profile page (used by both /u/:username and /profile), separate from Crates, with component tests and documentation updates.
tasks.description:
API (built by T1, already merged): `PublicProfile` from '@frisson/shared' now has `favorites: ProfileFavorite[]`, newest favorited first. `ProfileFavorite = { id: number; name: string; color: string; label: string | null; albumCount: number; ownerUsername: string | null; ownerDisplayName: string | null }` (owner fields are null for ownerless legacy crates). `crates` still lists owned crates only. The favorites list is public, so every viewer sees it. MyProfileView (/profile) renders ProfileView with the session user's username, so a change to ProfileView covers both routes. 1. apps/web/src/views/ProfileView.vue: after the existing `
`, add a separate `
` with `

Favorites

`. - Each favorite is an `
  • ` card built like the Crates cards: color swatch, then a RouterLink to `{ name: 'crate', params: { id } }` (class crate-link, aria-label from crateLinkName) showing label/name. Add a plain-text owner line, e.g. `by {{ fav.ownerDisplayName }}`, only when ownerDisplayName is non-null. Then the album count. - The owner must be text, not a link. The stretched-link ::after covers the card, so a nested link would be unreachable, and nested interactive content is not allowed. - Empty state: `

    No favorites yet.

    `. - Stretched-link containment is a known risk from earlier runs. Every card li needs position: relative (the existing .crate rule does this) so each ::after covers only its own card. Neither section may overlap the other, and nothing in the Favorites section may cover the Crates links. Long names and owner names wrap (overflow-wrap: anywhere) so neither 390px nor 1280px widths cause horizontal page overflow. - Render user text with {{ }} only, never v-html. Leave the Crates section, follow button and header as they are. 2. apps/web/src/views/ProfileView.test.ts (AC7). T1 already added `favorites: []` to the fixtures. Add tests: - A 'Favorites' heading exists and comes after the 'Crates' heading in document order, in its own section. - Each favorite links to /crates/:id and shows its owner's display name. - A favorited crate appears only under Favorites and not under Crates. - With no favorites, 'No favorites yet.' is shown. - A favorite with null owner fields renders without an owner line. 3. Docs: - README.md: API endpoint table gets PUT/DELETE /api/crates/:id/favorite (signed in, 204, idempotent; 400 own crate) and the viewerFavorited field on GET /api/crates/:id. The routes/features text mentions the Favorite button on /crates/:id and the Favorites section on profiles. - docs/SPEC.md: Data model gets crate_favorites (user_id, crate_id, created_at; unique pair; cascade on both FKs). Add the API and UI notes too. - docs/DEPLOY.md: upgrade note that migration 0006 adds the crate_favorites table and is additive. - New docs/adr/0008-public-crate-favorites.md in Context/Decision/Consequences format, matching the existing ADRs. It records that favorites are public on profiles (unlike follow lists), are only set by request.user, cannot target your own crate, and cascade on user or crate delete. Run `npm test -w apps/web`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and `npx prettier --check` on changed files from the repo root. Do not start a dev server or touch data/crate.db or .shipyard/. Commits: feat(web): ..., docs: ...
